title: Data Type Mismatch and Coercion Risks
description: Verification of semantic vs physical storage data types (e.g., numeric IDs stored as floats, dates as strings).
conditions: Numeric columns read as object/string due to currency symbols, commas, or error strings ('N/A', '#REF!')
Integer identifiers stored as float64 leading to precision loss on large 64-bit integers
Boolean columns represented as mixed integers, characters ('Y'/'N'), and True/False
recommended_methods: Regex-based character stripping before numeric coercion
Strict schema assertion with Pydantic / Pandera type validation
Safe casting with error interception ('coerce' vs 'raise')
selection_rules: If column is a discrete identifier (e.g. Patient ID, ZIP code), cast to string, never float
If column contains mixed numbers and strings, extract non-numeric tokens into separate error audit table
If boolean has > 2 non-null representations, map through explicit truth-value dictionary
limitations: Blind coercion with 'coerce=errors' silently replaces invalid data with NaN, hiding corruption
Memory explosion when casting sparse categorical strings to dense uncompressed object types
